thread.title: Stock Market Correction Back; Apple, Target, Crude Oil Fall: Weekly Review | Investor's Business Daily

author: IBD STAFF
title: Stock Market Correction Back; Apple, Target, Crude Oil Fall: Weekly Review | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market correction is back on as the Nasdaq undercut October lows with the S&P 500 index and Dow Jones also down sharply. Apple ( AAPL ) continued to hit new lows, but selling was broad-based. Target ( TGT ), Kohl's ( KSS ) and Ross Stores ( ROST ) plunged on earnings and guidance, continuing a recent tumble for the retail sector. Black Friday lured shoppers early Friday, though retailers offer ongoing holiday deals before and after, online and in stores. Energy stocks reeled as crude oil prices plunged to 52-week lows.
X Stock Market Correction Revived With the Nasdaq composite knifing below October lows, the other major averages suffering major losses and leading stocks struggling, the short-lived market uptrend failed and a new or revived stock market correction is underway. The Dow Jones lost 4.4%, the Nasdaq 4.3% and the S&P 500 3.8%. Apple and software stocks were among the big tech losers. Retailers plunged amid another fresh earnings reports and guidance. Crude oil prices plunged to 52-week lows, rocking energy stocks.
Target Misses, Kohl's Guidance Disappoints Discount giant Target 's ( TGT ) earnings and sales missed third-quarter estimates, with higher costs related to handling digital orders squeezing margins. Kohl's ( KSS ) earnings and sales topped but the value department store chain's raised guidance was below analysts' consensus. Target stock fell 15% and Kohl's 12%.
Ross Stores, TJX Cautious On Holidays Off-price heavyweights TJX ( TJX ) and Ross Stores ( ROST ) reported mixed Q3 results and cautious holiday-quarter guidance. T.J. Maxx parent TJX reported adjusted EPS of 54 cents, below estimates, while a 12% revenue gain to $9.83 billion topped. Ross Stores edged past EPS views while sales grew 7% to $3.35 billion, just missing. Freight costs and pay hikes weighed on results. Ross says it is up against its "toughest sales comparisons from 2017" and expects fierce competition. TJX stock tumbled 11% and Ross stock 16%.
Foot Locker Sprints On Earnings Athletic apparel and shoe retailer Foot Locker ( FL ) came out ahead of analyst forecasts, with profit up 9% to 95 cents a share and sales declining only 0.5% to $1.86 billion. Same-store sales rose 2.9%, ahead of estimates for 2% comps. The stock gapped up 15% Wednesday as shares continue to consolidate. Wedbush says Foot Locker's position is improving as it "remains a top destination for sneakerheads and a strong partner for multiple brands, including Nike."
Apparel Retailers Report Earnings Urban Outfitters ( URBN ) easily exceeded views as profit shot up 71% to 70 cents and sales grew 9% to $974 million. Comparable sales also topped. Shares rose modestly Tuesday. L Brands ( LB ) beat Q3 views and raised full-year profit outlook but shares plunged as the Victoria's Secret parent halved its annual dividend to $1.20. Meanwhile, Gap ( GPS ) cut its full-year profit guidance and is mulling closing hundreds of stores as Gap and Old Navy same-store sales underperformed expectations. But Gap, which slightly beat Q3 views, saw its stock rebound Wednesday and Friday from a 14-month low.
Best Buy Gives Muted Holiday Outlook The consumer electronics retailer beat Wall Street's targets for its fiscal third quarter ended Nov. 3. But it came up short with its holiday-quarter outlook. Best Buy ( BBY ) blamed its guidance miss on the fact that this year's fiscal fourth quarter has one less week than the same quarter last year. The retailer expects same-store sales growth to be flat to up 3% in the January quarter. CEO Hubert Joly said Best Buy is promoting many "exciting products" this year including big-screen TVs, smart speakers, security cameras, streaming devices and video games.
Chip Stocks Disappoint On Guidance Chip-gear maker Brooks Automation ( BRKS ) topped fiscal fourth-quarter views, but guided well below consensus for the current quarter. Chipmaker Analog Devices ( ADI ) beat Q4 views for its fiscal fourth quarter, but gave weak EPS guidance. Micron Technology ( MU ) fell on reports that it is one of several memory chipmakers that China's antitrust regulators are probing for possible anticompetitive activity. Nvidia ( NVDA ) rebounded from an 18-month low as Citron Research turned positive on the graphics chipmaker.
Crude Oil Plunges U.S. crude futures plunged to 52-week lows Tuesday as the stock market correction resumed, with energy groups big losers. President Donald Trump pressured Saudi Arabia on Twitter to keep oil prices down as OPEC's de facto leader weighs a production cut. America will "remain a steadfast partner of Saudi Arabia" despite reports that the CIA has concluded Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman was aware of, and perhaps responsible for, the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi. U.S. crude inventories rose for a ninth straight week, though gasoline stockpiles fell and crude production was flat week-over-week. Cimarex Energy ( XEC ) will buy Resolute Energy ( REN ) for $1.6 billion, including debt, to expand its acreage in the Permian Basin. The deal will add 35,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day to Cimarex production.
Housing Activity Sluggish The National Association of Home Builders' homebuilder sentiment gauge tumbled 8 points in November, to 60, the lowest point in two years. Weekly mortgage applications to buy a home fell 5% vs. a year earlier amid interest rate and affordability concerns. Existing-home sales rose 1.4% in September to a seasonally adjusted rate of 5.22 million, the first monthly gain in six months. Sales fell 5.1% vs. a year earlier. October housing starts rose 1.5% to a 1.228 million annualized pace, fueled by a jump in multifamily units. But they fell 2.9% vs. a year earlier. Separately, Lowe's ( LOW ) earnings topped views, but the home improvement chain cut full-year sales and same-store sales guidance.
JD.com Hits Record Low As Growth Slows Three China e-commerce companies checked in with third-quarter reports. JD.com ( JD ) reported revenue grew 25% to $15.3 billion, the slowest growth since its May 2014 IPO. JD founder and CEO Richard Liu, briefly arrested in Minneapolis in August on a rape claim, is stepping away from managing the core e-commerce business. Shares hit a record low. Pinduoduo ( PDD ) soared as the 2018 IPO reported a 700% revenue gain to $491 million with a smaller-than-expected per-share loss. Baozun ( BZUN ), which helps Western brands sell online in China, reported better-than-expected earnings with revenue up 25% to $161.7 million. Shares popped Wednesday but were little changed for the week.
News In Brief Car industry legend Carlos Ghosn was arrested in Japan on charges that he underreported his compensation for years. Ghosn built Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi into the world's biggest car alliance. Japan's Nissan ( NSANY ) removed Ghosn as chairman but France's Renault declined to oust him as chair or chief executive, highlighting apparent alliance strife. Ghosn had been pushing for a full Renault-Nissan merger. Nissan stock, already battered by slumping sedan sales, hit a multiyear low.
Boeing ( BA ) canceled a call with airlines over last month's Lion Air 737 Max crash amid reports that the aerospace giant didn't disclose to pilots safety issues with the newest Max. It's now planning meetings in various places with airlines and conference calls this coming week. Also, South Korea's Jeju Air Co. ordered 40 737 Max 8 jets, valued at $4.41 billion at list prices. Shares hit a 10-month low on Tuesday.
Medtronic ( MDT ) on Tuesday reported adjusted earnings of $1.22 per share on $7.48 billion in sales. The medical products giant topped views.
Deere ( DE ) saw EPS vault 47% to $2.30 on a revenue gain of 17% to $8.34 billion. It still missed lofty expectations, as material cost pressures continued. Deere stock rose 2.4% on Wednesday but fell for the week.
Niu Technologies ( NIU ) saw revenue jump 86% to $71.81 million. The Chinese electric scooter IPO posted a net loss of 1 cent a share. Niu Tech, which makes moped-like scooters, has its sights on the hot market for shared scooters and bikes.
Computer-aided design software firm Autodesk ( ADSK ) cheered investors with better-than-expected third-quarter results and fourth-quarter guidance. Shares popped 12% Wednesday but still fell 1% for the week.
